title: What is known about 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on: the structure of its run (two counters ticking together), the rules proved in Lean, and the open question.
verdict: The question is open. The machine runs two binary counters off one engine, one of them with stretches of junk between its digits. It can halt only if a carry finds a 1 where it has found a 0 every time so far. No halt in the first 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: Both counters' increments, for all sizes
claims.text: From the engine at cell 117: the left increment over n ones (12n+48 steps), the right increment on a lowest 0 (4 steps) and over k+1 ones (8k+12), the two most frequent left carries into the junk (144 and 108 steps, concrete), and m_e1_split, the two steps (E1 = 1RF, F0 = 1LA) where the run leaves the reference's. 6 theorems.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 256 cells have been visited and 101 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 1011 steps (longrun.c, the simulator of tools/c/tm.h) without a halt.

claims.title: E1 is rare
claims.text: E1 is used 62 times in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps; every other non-halting transition 10<sup>7</sup> to 2·10<sup>8</sup> times.

claims.title: How much of the run the increments cover
claims.text: In the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps (2,221,740 events at cell 117, from step 216,421) 95.4% of the events are instances of these theorems (left 911,530; right0 555,435; right1 555,435; junk_b 65,109; junk_a 32,555); the rest are deeper left carries into the junk and the transient before step 40,881,629.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.044). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Two counters of the same events
claims.text: Read off the run: the counters on the two sides of the engine both go up by 1 at every visit of the head to the engine, one of them with fixed junk stretches between some digits; the junk is written when a carry reaches the end of the tape.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if F reads a 1, i.e. only if after E1 (1RF) only the head finds a 1; it never has, and the layout of the junk, which would decide it, is not decoded.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine builds two binary counters that tick together, one on each side of an engine. Here the left one has stretches of junk between its digits. It would halt only if a carry ever found a 1 where it has always found a 0.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run.
Uses of E1, the only way into F.
The sweeps of the run, proved for every length.

sections.heading: Two counters and an engine
html:
Most of the time the tape is L · engine · R. Each visit of the head to the engine is an event, and every event adds 1 to both counters. In the reference machine of the family (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---), L is written in blocks of four cells, 0101 for a 1 and 0001 for a 0, lowest digit next to the engine, and R keeps one cell per digit, three cells apart (the cells 9, 12, 15, … right of the head), lowest digit nearest the engine. Nine consecutive events of the reference machine right after its left-end visit at step 1,571,372 (the head in state A on the bold cell):

(The block of L touching the engine is always 0001; the low bits shown are the next three blocks. The carries are sweeps proved in Lean for every length; in the reference machine r_up and r_down carry the right counter over k ones in 5k + 13 and 3k + 18 steps.)

This machine is the mirror case of the family: the same engine, but the junk sits between the digits of the left counter and the right counter is clean, and neither side is clockwork.

sections.heading: A counter with junk between its digits
html: The cells that change between events are the digits of the counters: each digit changes about half as often as the one before (chg.c counts, over a whole period, how often each cell changes from one event to the next). Here the junk is on the left: between some digits of L there are stretches of fixed cells that the carries cross without changing, and the right counter is clean. They are written when a carry runs into the end of the tape, at irregular event counts, and their layout is what makes the run irregular. How they are produced is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: The dangerous moments
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1, and F is entered from E1 (1RF) only. E1 is the rare transition here: 62 uses in the first 109 steps, each followed by F reading a 0 (F0 = 1LA, also 62 uses). So it halts only if one of these rare moments finds a 1. None of this has happened; whether the junk can ever arrange it is the open question.

sections.heading: Eight machines, one mechanism
html: The family (G11-Y): 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (the reference), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (the same run), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- (all with left-end extensions after 2k events, each twice, to within a few hundred steps of each other); 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- and 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- (the same right part, a differently written left counter); and the mirror case 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---, with the junk on the left.

sections.heading: The increments, proved for every size
html: This relative follows the reference machine for 87 steps; at the first use of E1 it writes a 1 the reference never writes (m_e1_split) and goes its own way. Its engine settles at cell 117 with a clean right counter (one cell per digit) and a left counter whose high part is a nest of further counters. lean/Events.lean proves the left and right increments for every size; in the first 3·108 steps 95.4% of the visits to the engine are instances of these theorems, the rest being carries deep into the nested left part.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Decode what a carry writes when it reaches the end of the tape, as a function of the counters, so that the layout of the junk after each visit is a formula. Then the question becomes whether a carry can ever find a 1 where it has always found a 0, which may be provable by an invariant of the junk, or may reduce to an arithmetic question about the two counters.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.044). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 256 cells (44 left of the start, 200 right), with a density of 1s of 0.395.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Two binary counters tick together off one engine; the left one has junk between its digits; it halts only if a carry finds a 1 where it has always found a 0 (family Y: the mirror case, D1 = 0RB, F0 = 1LA).
